---
title: Filter-authored severity highlighting
format: html
filters:
  - highlight-severity.lua
_quarto:
  tests:
    html:
      noErrors: true
      ensureFileRegexMatches:
        - ["hl-severity-err\">&lt;err&gt;</span>",
           "hl-severity-warning\">&lt;warning&gt;</span>",
           "hl-severity-info\">&lt;info&gt;</span>",
           "hl-timestamp\">Apr 21 12:34:56</span>",
           "<pre class=\"sourceCode systemd-log\""]
---

Filters aren't limited to literal-word matching. This document
demonstrates a **structured log highlighter** — a Lua filter that
matches timestamp prefixes and severity tags in journalctl-style
output and produces nested `<span>` annotations via `data-hl-spans`.

The filter is in `highlight-severity.lua`. It uses the idiomatic
`cb.attr.attributes["data-hl-spans"] = …` mutation pattern; no
`pandoc.Attr(…)` rebuild workaround is needed.

```systemd-log
Apr 21 12:34:56 host systemd[1]: <info> Starting service …
Apr 21 12:34:57 host app[123]: <warning> Retrying connection
Apr 21 12:34:58 host app[123]: <err> Connection refused
```

Every severity tag in `<…>` brackets gets its own capture
(`severity.err`, `severity.warning`, `severity.info`, …), and each
line's timestamp gets `timestamp`. Capture names with dots map to
HTML classes with hyphens (`severity.err` → `hl-severity-err`), so
users can style them with `.hl-severity-err { color: red; }` in
their own CSS.
